source.title: Treasury Mgmt Strategy 2026-27 — Full Council, 26 February 2026 (95085)

facts.note: Portfolio at 31/3/25: PWLB £32.638m (87.88%) + LOBOs £4.500m (12.12%) = £37.138m. At 30/9/25: PWLB £53.594m (92.25%) + LOBOs £4.500m (7.75%) = £58.094m. £20.956m of PWLB drawn in six months to 30/9/25. Forecast Debt at 1 April table: 37.138 (25/26 opening) → 134.935 (26/27 opening) → 174.678 (27/28 opening) → 196.696 (28/29 opening) → implied 224.064 by 31/3/29. Adding OLTL of ~£4.6m gives gross debt £228.711m at 31/3/29.

facts.value: £32.955m at 31/3/25 collapsing to ~£1m from 31/3/26 onwards — near-total closure of the internal-borrowing gap in one year
facts.note: Under/(over) borrowing: 32.955 (24/25 act) → 1.025 (25/26 est) → 1.025 (26/27 est) → 1.005 (27/28 est) → 1.004 (28/29 est). At 24/25 actual, external debt was 56% of CFR (£42.189m gross debt / £75.144m CFR). From 25/26 onwards the plan runs external debt to within £1m of CFR — functionally fully externally borrowed. Balance sheet identity ties in every year: CFR less external borrowing less OLTL = under/(over) borrowing to the £'000. Distinctive shape among the councils we have read — Camden runs £518m under-borrowed, Cheshire West £307m; most hold a substantial internal-borrowing position as a cost-of-carry hedge. Thanet's paper is explicit: 'the Council will continue to explore and utilise internal borrowing opportunities as appropriate to reduce its net interest cost' (§3.1.1).

facts.value: £4.5m LOBO position, unchanged across 31/3/25 and 30/9/25; call date and rate not disclosed in these papers
facts.note: LOBO share of external borrowing has shrunk from 12.12% at 31/3/25 to 7.75% at 30/9/25 purely because PWLB has grown; the £4.5m nominal is unchanged. No call date, lender or rate given in 95085/95115/95116. Such detail would be in the unheld Annex 1 (Prudential and Treasury Indicators appendix). Across the councils we have read this year we have logged 12 LOBO calls, all refused.

Operational Boundary 26/27: £214.000m total (debt £186m + OLTL £28m). Both tables include a £5m uplift to the debt line 'to provide additional capacity for any non-treasury investments that the Council may pursue' (p.12) — the paper is explicit that any such investments 'are not limited to £5m' and that the headroom 'has not been reflected elsewhere in this report, pending the formulation and approval of any such items'. So the CFR, external debt and financing tables do not include the £5m; the £5m sits only in the limit lines.

facts.value: Single-pool liability benchmark chart; External Loans (red) converges on Loans CFR (blue) at 31/3/26 and tracks it through 31/3/29
facts.note: Four-line chart: Loans CFR (blue, ceiling), External Loans (red, actual/planned), Net Loan Requirement (yellow, CFR less all treasury balances), Gross Loan Requirement (green, NLR + £10m liquidity buffer). At 31/3/25 the blue line sits ~£35m above the others; by 31/3/26 all four converge around £135m and External Loans tracks Loans CFR thereafter, with NLR/GLR sitting £20-30m below reflecting held balances. Single-pool treatment (unlike Slough's two-pool GF/HRA split). Chart shows the strategic decision to close the internal-borrowing gap over 25/26.

facts.value: Bank Rate to 3.25% by Sep-27, held to end-28; 10y PWLB to 4.80% by Sep-26 (vs today ~5.80%); table dated 11.08.25
facts.note: MUFG Corporate Markets Interest Rate View dated 11.08.25 printed in the strategy going to Council on 26 February 2026 (six months old at strategy time; twelve months old today, 2026-08-16). Bank Rate: 4.00 (Sep25) → 3.75 (Mar26) → 3.50 (Sep26 to Jun27) → 3.25 (Sep27 to Sep28). 10y PWLB: 5.30 (Sep25) → 5.00 (Mar26) → 4.80 (Sep26 held to Mar28) → 4.60 (Sep28). 25y PWLB: 6.10 (Sep25) → 5.50 (Sep26 held to Mar27) → 5.30 (Dec27 to Sep28). 50y PWLB: 5.80 → 5.30 → 5.00. Investment earnings (§4.4 p.20): 3.90% (25/26 res), 3.60% (26/27), 3.30% (27/28), 3.50% (28/29 to years 10+). §4.4 caveat honest: 'rates may be expected to fall throughout 2026, but only if the CPI measure of inflation maintains a downwards trend towards the Bank of England's 2% target'. Today's actuals (per recent notes 2026-08-12/14): Bank Rate 3.75% (25bp above Sep-26 forecast point); 10y PWLB certainty 5.80% (100bp above); 20y PWLB certainty 6.34% (80bp above the 25y forecast point of 5.50). Divergence widens from short end to medium end of curve.

facts.value: Pre-2008 supported capex: 4% of GF CFR (existing practice). Post-2008 unsupported: asset life straight line. HRA: no MRP.
facts.note: Standard asset-life straight line for post-March 2008 unsupported borrowing (§2.4). No PWLB-rate-linked annuity method — simpler than Slough's or Tower Hamlets' approach. Reg 27(3): MRP delayed until year following the year of expenditure. Capital expenditure financed by borrowing in 2025/26 not charged MRP until 2026/27, or year following when the asset first becomes available for use. Capitalisation Direction MRP: asset life method applied. VRP permitted, can be reclaimed subject to disclosure of cumulative overpayment. Loans to third parties: capital receipts from principal repayments may reduce CFR instead of MRP.

facts.value: £38.187m at 30/9/25 (£2.203m banks + £33.984m MMFs + £2.000m bond fund); £35.000m assumed throughout 26/27 to 28/29
facts.note: §2.3 Year End Resources at 24/25: Fund balances/reserves £20.460m + Capital receipts £7.865m + Earmarked reserves £8.163m = Total core funds £36.488m. Falls to £13.227m by 28/29 (fund balances £7.227m + capital receipts £2.000m + earmarked £4.000m). Expected investments held flat at £35.000m 26/27 to 28/29. Ratio moves from 'net investor of £1.746m at 31/3/25' to 'net borrower of £19.907m at 30/9/25' — swing of £18.161m in six months, driven by PWLB drawdown of £20.956m. Non-specified investment limit £5m; longer-than-365-days limit £5m (position 30/9/25: £nil). £2m in a bond fund classified as longer-term for TMSS purposes though held for cash-flow with 2-day settlement (§4.4 p.20).

25/26 capex is 3.83x the 24/25 actual, driving the £65.5m CFR movement. HRA share dominates 25/26 (£79.981m of £159.563m = 50%) and remains substantial in outer years (30-34m). Net financing need for year: 15.099 (24/25) → 67.188 (25/26) → 42.471 (26/27) → 25.468 (27/28) → 31.284 (28/29). Financing mix 26/27: capital receipts £1.6m (GF+HRA); grants/contributions £24.279m; reserves £9.851m; HRA revenue £0.250m; 'Other - HRA' £7.500m; net financing need £42.471m.

summary.text:
A small Kent district planning to become a materially larger borrower over four years — one of the sharpest CFR trajectories we've read this strategy season. CFR moves from £75.144m at 31/3/25 to £229.715m at 31/3/29, growing by £65.5m in 25/26 alone. External debt is forecast to follow it exactly: gross debt £42.189m at 31/3/25 rising to £228.711m at 31/3/29, closing the £32.955m under-borrowing gap from 25/26 and running within £1m of CFR every year thereafter. The transition is deliberate — the paper's §3.1.1 flags that External Loans are 'projected to approach the Loans CFR in future years, ensuring that external loan balances and interest are factored into budgets' — but among the councils we've read the shape is unusual: most authorities carry substantial internal borrowing as a cost-of-carry hedge (Camden runs £518m under-borrowed, Cheshire West £307m). Thanet is closing that hedge.

The 25/26 CFR jump is driven by a capital programme (§2.1) that steps from £41.676m (24/25 actual) to £159.563m (25/26 budget) — a 3.83x jump — before easing to £85.951m in 26/27 and £50-£55m thereafter. HRA is half of the 25/26 programme (£79.981m) and remains at £30m+ per year in the outer years, so HRA CFR grows from £42.708m to £126.410m across the plan.

The MUFG forecast printed in §3.3 is dated 11.08.25 — six months old at strategy time and twelve months old today. It has Bank Rate at 3.50% by September 2026 (one month out from now); actual Bank Rate is still 3.75%, held since December 2025. The 10-year PWLB certainty rate is 4.80% in the forecast for Sep-26; today it prints around 5.80% — a 100bp gap. The 25-year is 5.50% forecast vs ~6.34% at 20y today. The Council's own §4.4 caveat is honest — 'rates may be expected to fall throughout 2026, but only if the CPI measure of inflation maintains a downwards trend towards the Bank of England's 2% target' — and inflation hasn't done that. The paper does not print a single 'new-borrowing rate assumption' number; the borrowing strategy at §3.4 is a philosophy statement (postpone if rates fall sharply; re-appraise if they rise sharply) rather than a rate bet.

MRP policy is asset-life straight line for post-March 2008 unsupported borrowing (§2.4), no PWLB-rate-linked annuity method — simpler than Slough's or Tower Hamlets'. HRA carries no MRP, per statutory depreciation and the Major Repairs Reserve. Reg 27(3) delay applied — 25/26 borrowing not charged MRP until 26/27.

Balance sheet identity (CFR − external borrowing − OLTL = under/(over) borrowing) ties to the £'000 in every year of the plan: 24/25 75.144−37.138−5.051 = 32.955 (paper 32.955); 25/26 140.641−134.935−4.681 = 1.025 (paper 1.025); and so on through 28/29. Composition ties too: PWLB 32.638 + LOBOs 4.500 = 37.138 at 31/3/25; PWLB 53.594 + LOBOs 4.500 = 58.094 at 30/9/25. Note the paper is explicit that the £5m non-treasury investment headroom in the Authorised Limit is not reflected elsewhere in the report, pending formulation and approval of any specific item — the CFR and debt tables don't carry the £5m.

LOBO position is £4.5m, unchanged across the plan. No call date, lender or rate visible in 95085, 95115 or 95116 — that detail would sit in the unheld Annex 1 (Prudential and Treasury Indicators). Across the councils we've read this year, 12 LOBO calls have landed and every one has been declined by the lender. Not a lead for Thanet given the position is small and shrinking as a share of external debt.

Reconciliation with our PWLB file FAILS at 30/9/25. Our file returns 'no loans outstanding' at that date; paper §3.1 prints PWLB £53.594m. Live snapshot today shows 14 loans of £77.6m at weighted 4.51%, all of them drawn after 30/9/25 — the file captures the recent drawings the paper's plan requires (£81.5m of PWLB in the six months to 31/3/26) but not the pre-existing tail. Same shape as Slough, Leicester and Redcar. Recorded in the note per PIPELINE.md; kept out of the email; coverage gap disclosed once in the draft without inviting a correction. Break-cost output (14 live loans, ~£788k indicative net discount) held for internal reference only. Email leans on qualitative content: the trajectory of the borrowing programme, the MUFG forecast against actual, the internal-borrowing gap closure, and the liability benchmark chart.

officer.subject: Your CFR triples to £230m by 2028/29 — the trajectory and the transition
officer.body:
Dear Section 151 Officer,

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's premature-repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are a few thoughts on the Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 that went to Full Council on 26 February. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it. Your strategy is unusually candid about the scale of what you're planning, and this is offered in that spirit rather than as a critique.

What drew our attention first is the trajectory. Your CFR moves from £75.144m at 31 March 2025 to £229.715m by 31 March 2029 — a 3.06x increase over four years — with £65.5m of it added in 25/26 alone. Among the districts we've read, most run CFR growth in single digits and hold it there. Yours is driven by a capital programme (§2.1) that steps from £41.676m in 24/25 actual to £159.563m in 25/26 budget, half of it HRA.

The transition alongside it is the second thing. External debt of £42.189m at 31/3/25 was 56% of CFR — a substantial under-borrowed position of about £33m. From 25/26 onwards your plan runs external debt to within £1m of CFR every year through 28/29. Most of the councils we've read hold substantial internal borrowing as a cost-of-carry hedge (Camden £518m, Cheshire West around £307m). Your §3.1.1 is explicit about the reasoning, and the balance sheet identity ties to the pound in every year of the plan.

The MUFG forecast at §3.3 is dated 11 August 2025 — twelve months old now. It has Bank Rate at 3.50% by September 2026, a month from now; actual has been at 3.75% since December 2025. Ten-year PWLB certainty is 4.80% in the forecast for September 2026; today it sits around 5.80%, a 100bp gap. Twenty-five year is 5.50% forecast against about 6.34% at the twenty-year today. The gap widens from short to medium end, so the market has re-priced the terminal rate rather than doubting the next cut. Your §4.4 caveat was honest — rates would fall 'only if the CPI measure of inflation maintains a downwards trend towards the Bank of England's 2% target' — and it hasn't yet. On the £39.7m of new PWLB planned for 26/27, 100bp above the printed forecast is on the order of £400k a year in interest before it works itself back down. The full curve is at pwlbtoday.org/dashboard.

Where you might find us most useful day-to-day is at pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis, which prices every published council's PWLB book against the DMO's premature-repayment curve. One caveat before you look — our file for Thanet is missing the pre-September 2025 PWLB tail, the same gap we've seen at Slough, Leicester and Redcar. Anything drawn during this strategy period, and the monthly sector totals at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity, we can benchmark with confidence — and given the scale of what you're planning to draw, that is where the platform earns its keep for a book like yours.

Standing point, because CIPFA's forthcoming Prudential and Treasury Code updates will put it in front of every S151: the liability benchmark pathway is becoming central to how the whole strategy is framed. Your single-pool chart at §3.1.1 is one of the clearer presentations we've read — the four-line shape puts the strategic decision on one page. An interactive version tied to our live rate feeds sits at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity — being able to move the reserves and cost-of-carry paths and see the External Loans line shift is the useful part.

On training, four look most relevant to Thanet. PWLB strategy is written for a programme this size. Liability benchmark modelling covers the exact chart shape at §3.1.1. LA-to-LA borrowing market matters given §3.7 lists local authorities as an approved source. MRP — policy options and revenue impact is included because as the CFR grows, MRP starts to dominate revenue conversations even under a straightforward asset-life policy. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts are available for the whole team.

And if any of it is useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
https://www.linkedin.com/in/russelltew

Sources: Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 and its Annexes 2 and 3 — Full Council, 26 February 2026. At https://Thanet.moderngov.co.uk/documents/s95085/treasury-mgmt-strategy-2026-27.pdf and https://Thanet.moderngov.co.uk/documents/s95115/annex-2-treasury-management-practice-tmp.pdf and https://Thanet.moderngov.co.uk/documents/s95116/annex-3-guidance-on-treasury-management-strategy-statement-m.pdf.
